note: FULL run by Anurag on his MacBook Air, 2026-11-14, NR_MODEL_MODE=ollama, all 24 queries (8 easy/8 medium/8 hard). Real measured results. This supersedes the pilot-9 numbers for resume/hackathon claims.
reading: Defensible claim vs always-large: -59% latency at near-equal quality (0.95 vs 0.98), 24/24 routing. Token savings vs large are small (6.4%) because the hard path pays for retrieval + verifier + occasional escalation on top of the large model, and ad-hoc verification on medium queries adds verifier tokens. Vs always-medium, NeuroRoute is slower/pricier but higher quality (0.95 vs 0.92) - the quality-per-cost frontier argument. Known levers to improve before the hackathon: gate ad-hoc verification tighter, cap per-tier generation length (small model sometimes rambles, e.g. easy_3 524 tok in the live run).
